business_problem: Sibionics was iterating AI-assisted chronic-disease services such as intelligent Q&A and educational recommendations, but its previous fixed-server architecture slowed testing and training. The company also wasted resources during low traffic and still risked instability when pulse traffic arrived.
solution_summary: Sibionics moved its diabetes-focused AI services onto Alibaba Cloud ACK with Knative so product teams could release and scale medical-assistance workloads with less infrastructure friction. Knative gives the company a fast way to deploy service revisions to Kubernetes during frequent testing cycles, which matters because intelligent Q&A and related patient-support products require ongoing iteration. The same serverless layer also brings elastic scaling for spiky usage, queue-proxy request observation, and request-based gray release with multi-version management, so Sibionics can publish updates throughout the day without rebuilding its whole operations model. On top of that base, the company runs a diabetes intelligent Q&A system, a science-article recommendation system, blood-glucose and AGP analysis assistants, and a diabetes-event knowledge-graph labeling platform. The result is a fully serverless medical AI service layer rather than a collection of fixed-capacity application servers.

solution_components.name: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK)
solution_components.role: Provides the Kubernetes platform that hosts Sibionics' diabetes AI services.

solution_components.name: Knative
solution_components.role: Adds fast service deployment, elastic scaling, queue observation, and multi-version release controls.

data_flow: Medical-support requests are sent to Sibionics' Knative services on ACK, where the platform scales with demand and routes traffic to the current model version. The resulting Q&A answers, article recommendations, glucose analyses, and labeled event data are then fed back into patient-support and research workflows.
business_outcome: Sibionics removed much of the deployment overhead around chronic-disease AI services and gained a release model that better fits frequent experimentation and fluctuating traffic. The platform now supports a growing diabetes knowledge base and several patient-facing or clinician-support assistants on a fully serverless foundation.
metrics: diabetes Q&A system has collected more than 140,000 Q&A pairs
architecture_clues: Sibionics uses one Knative substrate for both interactive Q&A and background knowledge or labeling services.
Queue-proxy traffic observation and multi-version release management are part of the production medical-AI workflow.
The serverless design is used to support both patient-facing education scenarios and internal knowledge-graph preparation.
